problem: VLM-based indoor navigation is too slow on embedded hardware, since it re-invokes the VLM on every frame. Geometric/SLAM pipelines and reactive VLAs cannot read distant signs or reason about unseen intersections, and compact on-device VLMs lack spatial and textual grounding.
motivation: Indoor robots must react in real time on low-cost hardware such as a Jetson without cloud connectivity, but semantic cues like room numbers and signs need VLM-level reasoning. Preliminary experiments show the VLM emits identical decisions across hundreds of consecutive straight-hallway frames, and meaningful changes occur only at corners and intersections, so most VLM calls are redundant.
key_idea: Split navigation into a fast System One (patch-level key-frame gating, segmentation+OCR scene descriptions, and a precomputed condition-to-action table) and a slow System Two (a compact VLM called only for ambiguous cases, with spatial/textual cues injected into its prompt).
insight: Most navigation decisions are low-ambiguity and can be handled by lightweight matching (System One handled 53.6% of decisions), giving a bimodal latency of <1 s vs ~20 s. Segmentation+OCR condition matching reaches 87.5% accuracy versus <50% for VE-embedding similarity (CLIP/SigLIP/BLIP-2). Spatial/textual prompt augmentation lifts the compact VLM's decision accuracy from 48.2% to 64.3%. A deliberately conservative gate gave 100% recall for necessary turnovers at the cost of ~35% false-positive deferrals.
method: Key Frame Compare (KFC): SigLIP patch-level embeddings are compared against the last decision frame. System Two is triggered only when structural change exceeds a threshold (45% works best across sites).

Spatial/textual understanding: SegFormer-b0 masks plus vanishing-point ray partitioning give front/left/right/down and immediate/distant zones. docTR OCR extracts signs and room numbers. Both become text descriptions.

Condition Matching: the descriptions are matched by cosine similarity to a Condition-to-Action table to form a UniqueActions set. Exactly one action is executed. Zero or several are escalated to System Two. Destination arrival requires vision-text similarity >80% plus OCR of the destination text, then Idle.

Offline Condition-to-Action generation: at trip start the VLM (Gemma3-4B) sees the start image and goal description and speculatively generates 6-9 condition-action pairs in a strict, validated format, taking 25-33 s.

Additional Thinking: the VLM gets the goal, current image, and System One's spatial/textual cues. It has a 150-token budget, logit processing that suppresses non-action tokens after ~80% of the budget, and K-V cache restore and resume if no action is produced.

Execution Module: a finite-state Action Executor (Forward, CW(N°), CCW(N°), Turn Back) with a VP Tracker that picks a vanishing-point direction and steers to it (PID). Ultrasonic sensors give emergency stop.

setting.backbone: Gemma3-4B (frozen, System Two) + SigLIP encoder, SegFormer-b0, docTR OCR (all pretrained, System One)
setting.observation: three wide-angle RGB cameras (front, left, right)
setting.action_space: discrete high-level actions: Forward, CW(N°), CCW(N°), Turn Back, Idle, executed by VP tracking + PID
setting.privileged: none (floor map with start/goal is used only for human-labelled ground truth in evaluation)

numbers.eval_set_note: 120 episodes (10 per source-destination pair) over 5 buildings, 2,455 m of footage; results pooled across environments
numbers.extra: Human-consensus action labels as ground truth; single floor per building; fixed start locations
numbers.evidence: "significantly higher end-to-end complete episode success rate of 67.5% (11.5x than 5.83% for VLM only)"; "System One was responsible for 53.6% of all navigational decisions"; abstract: "reduces latency by 66%"

numbers.eval_set_note: same 120 episodes; System Two prompt ablation on decision accuracy
numbers.method: Gemma3-4B with Spatial & Textual Augmentation (System Two component)
numbers.evidence: intro: "improves the VLM's maneuver decision accuracy from 48.2% to 64.3%"

numbers_note: No standard benchmarks. Most results are in figures (latency-accuracy plots, confusion matrix); only text-stated values are captured. The 60% travel-time saving comes from a single 16.5 m path (240 s vs a >600 s VLM-only failure).
results: On a Jetson Orin NX across five real buildings, IROS reaches 67.5% end-to-end episode success versus 5.83% for the VLM-only Gemma3-4B baseline. It cuts latency by about 66%, and System One handles 53.6% of decisions at 0.7-0.9 s. Segmentation+OCR matching reaches 87.5% accuracy versus <50% for CLIP/SigLIP/BLIP-2 embedding matching.
limitations: Evaluation is only on the authors' own robot and buildings, on a single floor, with no standard benchmark or external baselines beyond a VLM-only variant.
No obstacle-avoidance or safety module and no validation in dynamic scenes; spatial/textual cues are injected only as text, which the compact VLM sometimes misreads.
System Two latency is still ~17-20 s per call, System One defers ~35% of manageable cases, and ~13 of 16 GB of memory is used.
